page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no marginal notes. The catchword CON- stands at the lower right.

main_text.p: quasi vermis in ligno: Sin heimlichs leyden[?], quod palàm conqueri non audet, vel potest, animo autem semper sentit, & ferre cogitur, sicuti nec calcei preffura cernitur, quantumlibet elegantis & prementis.
Interim tamen vt membrum corporis, nō ideó abijcitur, quia pus habet, sed potius sanatur: sic & vxor non repudianda propter quaedam vitia, sed potius modestè corrigenda, vel patienter ferenda.

3 Quomodo spiritualiter illud dictum est intelligendum? Si per mulierem ecclesi-am, & per virum Christum Dominum & magistrum & caput nostrum intelligas, Eph. 5. Debet enim ecclesia operam dare, vt corde, ore, & corpore, hoc est, fide, confessione, & operibus bonis, caput suum ornet atque glorificet, Rom. 4. Psal. 34. Matth. 5. eiusque nomen non blasphemet, Rom. 2. Nam quicunque honorificauerit me (inquit Dominus 1. Reg. 2.) glorificabo eum: qui autem contemnunt me, erunt ignobiles. Ille idem Dominus suam largia: ur nobis gratiam, vt in illis nostris diebus ita credamus, loquamur & viuamus, vt in die Domini resurgere possimus non ad ignominiam & opprobrium, sed ad vitam & gloriam sempiternam, A-men.

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment, "quafi", and continues from the previous page. The black-letter words "Sin heimlichs leyden" are set in Gothic type inside roman text; "heimlichs" is doubtful. "largia: ur" shows a colon-like mark at the line end where a hyphen would be expected; it is copied as printed. "ideó" and "nō" carry accent or stroke marks as printed. The "3" opening the third paragraph is a paragraph number and is not a heading. Possible printing errors: "Matth." and "Pfal." (printed "Pfal." in the scan) are copied as "Psal." only where the print clearly shows it; the scan is slightly blurred at the line ends.
